data.exact_reserve_text: 2022 is the YOA closing at this point with an NCOR of 96.6% which is 8.0pp above plan. Given that we experienced the effects of Hurricane Ian, the second largest insured catastrophe loss of all time, the outbreak of the Ukrainian War with Russia, and the heights of the post-Covid inflationary environment that year, with a particularly strong impact on the construction segments of our portfolio, being able to post a strongly positive result reflects the robustness of the model that we have been working so hard to develop. YOA 2023 is running relatively favourably against plan at this stage with a 93.0% NCOR against a plan of 91.8% despite a 19% shortfall in gross written premiums against plan as our underwriters strive to achieve the profitability ambitions of their plans rather than top line growth.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced mixed prior year development. The 2022 Year of Account closed with an NCOR 8.0 percentage points above plan, indicating adverse development, influenced by Hurricane Ian, the Ukrainian War, and post-Covid inflationary pressures impacting construction. However, the report also notes a 'strongly positive result' for 2022 and prior years due to an external Reinsurance-to-Close. The 2023 Year of Account is running 'relatively favourably against plan', despite its NCOR being above plan, and was impacted by significant insured market losses from severe convective storms in the US, Hurricane Idalia, Hawaii wildfires, Australia/New Zealand cyclones and flooding, the Turkish earthquake, and the early 2024 Baltimore Bridge collapse.
